subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence.

He was alone and knew the dangers ahead during his journey, but he __tried to keep up his confidence.__
solution: The correct answer is: **whistled in the dark**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The phrase **"to keep up his confidence"** refers to maintaining one's self-assurance and belief in oneself despite challenging circumstances. (आत्मविश्वास बनाए रखना) • **Example: **Even when the odds were against her, she did everything she could to keep up her confidence. • **"Whistled in the dark" **is an idiom that means trying to remain brave or pretending to be unafraid in a scary or uncertain situation; it implies an attempt to keep up one's spirits. (डर के बावजूद साहस बनाए रखना) • **Example: **He whistled in the dark as he walked through the abandoned house, trying not to let his fear show. • Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom for "tried to keep up his confidence" is "whistled in the dark". Therefore, the correct answer is: **whistled in the dark**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Made of sterner stuff **(अधिक मजबूत बनाया गया): Refers to someone who is very strong in character, especially in a difficult situation. • **Example:** Despite the setbacks, she proved she was made of sterner stuff and persevered. • **Stepped up his game **(अपने खेल को बेहतर बनाया): To improve performance or quality in response to a challenge. • **Example: **After receiving feedback, he stepped up his game and delivered an outstanding presentation. • **Wouldn’t be caught dead** (किसी भी स्थिति में नहीं पाया जाएगा): Used to express strong dislike or disapproval towards something. • **Example:** He’s so particular about his appearance; he wouldn’t be caught dead wearing something out of fashion. 3f:T990, The correct answer is: **Nervous**.
